newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel TV report disrupts cabinet vote on deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel TV report disrupts cabinet vote on deal.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu interrupted a stormy cabinet debate on the Hebron accord on Wednesday to check a TV report seized on by hardliners as a reason to scupper the deal, which was later rectracted.

The report on Israel's Channel One Television quoted a State Department spokesman as saying Israel would not on its own decide how much future West Bank land it would give Palestinians -- but would have to negotiate the issue with the PLO.
The report was dismissed by the U.S. State Department, and later retracted by Israel Television's Washington reporter.

Cabinet ministers, enraged by the report, demanded an explanation, especially since Israeli officials had insisted earlier that a U.S. letter of guarantees stated Israel would define the depth of the three additional West Bank pullbacks.

But the meeting resumed a short time later after Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh checked the televised report with U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who assured him this was not the view of the U.S. administration, Israel Radio said.

Deputy State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said later: "That was not what was said -- that the question of Israeli withdrawals will be a subject for bilateral negotiation...The report that was on Israeli Channel One was erroneous."

The cabinet meeting, called by Netanyahu to approve the deal giving Palestinians self-rule in 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron, ran over schedule as at least seven of his 18 cabinet ministers opposed it.
Netanyahu cancelled a news conference he had planned to hold following the cabinet meeting as the debate continued.
Before the cabinet meeting, Indyk confirmed that the area to be handed to the PLO in the three subsequent redeployments "is, according to the agreement, Israel's decision".
Netanyahu's adviser Dore Gold said of the U.S. guarantee: "It helps establish that the redeployment process is a unilateral process by Israel."

In Gaza, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's cabinet approved the accord on Wednesday night, Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo told reporters. Details of the vote were not immediately available.
